title: Sensitive-data redaction shim and audit-event channel for embeddings/rerank
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Background: Embedding and rerank requests sometimes contain customer PII or other sensitive attributes. Current request tracing and debug logs retain raw request payloads in internal telemetry streams for short troubleshooting windows, but we lack a consistent, configurable mechanism to prevent sensitive content from being persisted or to create an auditable, privacy-preserving trail for compliance requests.

Goal: Provide a pluggable 'redaction shim' at the embeddings/rerank ingress that applies deterministic or irreversible redaction per-customer, emits structured audit events (schema-backed) to a separate audit pipeline, and exposes per-customer controls for retention and logging level. The solution must preserve reranking quality for customers who opt into non-redaction while allowing strict no-PII retention modes for regulated customers.

High-level approach: implement a lightweight ingress middleware that inspects incoming embedding/rerank payloads and applies one of three modes: 'none' (no transformation), 'hash' (deterministic HMAC per-customer using KMS-derived key), or 'redact' (replace detected sensitive spans with placeholders). The shim will also emit a compact audit event for each request to an audit topic (separate from standard telemetry) containing metadata (customer id, route, transformation mode, fingerprint/hint) but never raw sensitive text. Retention of audit events will be configurable per-tenant with a default of 30 days and options down to 0 days (immediate purge) for customers with strict requirements.

Constraints and non-goals: we will not store or ship raw PII to downstream long-term analytics buckets. This ticket does not change model training data handling. We will not implement a full DLP engine; initial sensitive span detection will use an ensemble of regexes + a light ML detector to catch emails, SSNs, phone numbers, credit card formats and named-entity PERSON when found in short payloads.

Acceptance criteria: see 'acceptance_criteria' field.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress shim integrated with embeddings and rerank endpoints and selectable per-API-key via customer config
Three transformation modes supported: none, hash (deterministic HMAC), redact (placeholder), default to 'hash' for new tenants
Audit event schema defined and produced to audit topic; events contain no raw sensitive spans
Per-tenant retention config implemented with admin console toggle; default retention 30 days, min 0 days
E2E tests that verify that redacted requests never appear in long-term logs and that hashed values are stable across requests for same input and tenant
Benchmarks demonstrating <5% p99 latency regression on rerank happy path at 99th percentile for typical payload sizes (<=1024 tokens)
Security review completed and design doc signed off by Security and Compliance
Runbook that describes how to respond to retention/forensics requests and how to rotate HMAC keys
tasks: Design: final schema for audit events and retention metadata (confluence link in links)
Infra: audit-topic provisioning and access controls (separate from standard telemetry)
Runtime: implement redaction shim in inference gateway with mode flag per-api-key
Security: integrate HMAC key derivation via KMS, implement key rotation path
Detectors: implement lightweight regex + ML ensemble detector (configurable thresholds)
E2E: unit + integration tests and synthetic replay tests to validate no raw PII leaks
Telemetry: dashboards for counts by transformation mode and retention expirations
Rollout: canary plan and fallback (automatic degrade to 'hash' if detector OOMs)

2025-03-04 - Marco: Began feature-flagged rollout in staging; audit events flowing into audit-topic (arn:audit:staging:embedding-shim). PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-inference/pull/4381, https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2107
metrics: logs.pii_leak_detection - synthetic tests for raw PII in long-term buckets (must be zero)
notes: Implementation detail: use HMAC-SHA256 with tenant-scoped salt pulled from KMS. Store only the HMAC digest in logs; do not persist salts or unhashed spans.
Policy: default tenant profile will be 'hash' to balance debugging and privacy; customers can request 'redact' or 'none' via contract.
Rollout: start with non-sensitive tenants in staging, then internal Canary with <5% of production traffic, monitor leakage tests closely.
Open question: downstream analytics teams need access to hashed tokens for aggregation. We will provide an allowlist mechanism and separate RBAC-controlled export if needed.
